refnamediv.refpurpose: Enable, disable, stop, and restart units when packages are installed, upgraded, or removed

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: Package managers call systemd-update-helper from the scriptlets of packages that contain unit files. The systemd RPM macros and file triggers call it. It has to run as root.

By default, the commands operate on the system service manager and the system unit directories. With --global, they operate on the global user unit configuration and on every running user service manager, i.e. every active user@UID.service unit. A user service manager that fails or does not finish the operation within 15 seconds is skipped and does not affect the others. The timeout is set at build time with the -Dupdate-helper-user-timeout-sec= option.

If the system was not booted with systemd, or the helper runs in a chroot2 environment, the commands only change unit files and skip all operations on service managers. Set $SYSTEMD_OFFLINE= to override this detection, see Known Environment Variables.

A UNIT argument is either a unit name or the absolute path of a unit file directly in /usr/lib/systemd/system/ or /etc/systemd/system/, or in /usr/lib/systemd/user/ or /etc/systemd/user/ with --global. The path does not have to exist. Template units passed to remove-units, mark-restart-units, and mark-reload-units apply to all active instances of the template.

listitem.para: Enables or disables the units according to the preset policy, like systemctl preset does. With --global, applies the user preset policy to the global user unit configuration, like systemctl --global preset does.
Disables the units and stops them. With --global, each running user service manager also disables the units in the configuration of its user, where systemctl --user enable creates its symlinks.
Marks the units to be restarted or reloaded by the next enqueue-marked. See enqueue-marked in systemctl1.
Reloads the configuration of the service manager. With --global, reloads every running user service manager.
Restarts or reloads the units that are marked for it, and waits for the jobs to finish.
Operates on the system service manager and the system unit directories. This is the default.
Operates on the global user unit configuration and on every running user service manager.

Reads the units from standard input, one unit name or unit file path per line, instead of from the arguments. Lines that do not name a unit, or name a path outside of the unit directories, are ignored. The RPM file triggers pass the unit files of removed packages this way.
Logs the changes and operations without performing them.

refsect1.title: Exit status
refsect1.para: On success, 0 is returned, a non-zero failure code otherwise. A failure to preset a unit with install-units makes the command fail. Failures to disable, stop, mark, restart, or reload individual units, and failures of individual user service managers, are logged and do not change the exit status.

example.title: Disable and stop the units of a removed package
example.para: This disables sshd.service and sshd@.service, and stops sshd.service and all active instances of sshd@.service.
